name: Paul Jaboulet Aîné Crozes-Hermitage Domaine de Thalabert 2015
text:
## Paul Jaboulet Aîné Crozes-Hermitage Domaine de Thalabert 2015

**The story.** Paul Jaboulet Aîné, based at [Tain-l'Hermitage](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Paul+Jaboulet+A%C3%AEn%C3%A9,+Tain-l'Hermitage,+France&t=k), is one of the great names of the northern Rhône. It owns the little chapel on top of the [Hermitage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermitage_AOC) hill, built, legend says, where the wounded knight Gaspard de Stérimberg lived as a hermit after returning from the [Albigensian Crusade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albigensian_Crusade) in 1224 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermitage_AOC)).

**The wine: Domaine de Thalabert.** Thalabert is Jaboulet's [Crozes-Hermitage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crozes-Hermitage_AOC) from its own Domaine de Thalabert, made from [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah), the grape of nearly all red Crozes ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crozes-Hermitage_AOC)). For 2015, Jeb Dunnuck reports it was raised in a mix of tronconic (tapered) wooden vats and Burgundy barrels, 20% new ([Bordeaux Index, critics' notes](https://bordeauxindex.com/fine-wine/france/rhone/jabt-2015)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [northern Rhône vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/northern-rhone) calls 2015 "universally viewed as a vintage with top quality potential", though overshadowed by 2016 and 2017; with such ripe fruit, keeping freshness and avoiding over-extraction was the key. Dunnuck went further: "The 2015 reds from the Northern Rhône are truly spectacular", rivalling or surpassing 2010 and 2009.

**What the critics say for 2015.** As listed by [Bordeaux Index](https://bordeauxindex.com/fine-wine/france/rhone/jabt-2015) and [Fine Wine Cellar](https://www.finewinecellar.co.uk/products/crozes-hermitage-domaine-de-thalabert-domaine-paul-jaboulet-aine-2015):
- **[Jeb Dunnuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Dunnuck): 97** (January 2018). "The finest vintage to date, better even than the stellar 2010": blackcurrants, olive tapenade, truffles and earth; full-bodied, seamless, with fine tannin and no hard edges. Drink now or cellar 15 to 20 years.
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 93+** (Joe Czerwinski, December 2017). "A super effort, packed with savory notes of black olives and crushed stones"; full-bodied and rich with a hint of cedar. "Should drink well for a couple of decades." Drink 2020 to 2035.
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 93 to 95** (Jeb Dunnuck, from barrel, December 2016). Scorched earth, black fruit, cassis, black olive and graphite, like a slightly softer 2010; "you'll need to forget bottles for 4-5 years, but it will have over two decades of longevity".
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 91.1** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eleven years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2023 to 2030, and the Wine Advocate's runs to 2035. So it is in its prime: cassis, black olive, earth and smoke. Decant an hour ahead and serve at 16 to 17°C.

**Food.** Northern Rhône Syrah loves lamb with olives, a peppered steak, venison or duck.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Thalabert at the moment.

**From the history books**
- **A royal wine.** [Louis XIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XIII) made Hermitage a wine of the court after tasting it in 1642, and [Louis XIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XIV) sent [Charles II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_II_of_England) 200 casks of fine wine including Hermitage ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermitage_AOC)).
- **"Hermitaged."** In the 19th century Bordeaux wines were often blended with Hermitage, "hermitagé", to sell for higher prices ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermitage_AOC)).

**Curious details**
- **Crozes, Hermitage's big neighbour.** Crozes-Hermitage is the northern Rhône's largest appellation, about half the region's vineyards; in 1846 tasters already praised its likeness to Hermitage ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crozes-Hermitage_AOC)).
